templates.headline: BUDDY / SOLO ATHLETE

templates.name: Coach whistle confiscated
templates.what: Nudges have started sounding like supervision, disappointment, or commentary on effort and bodies.
templates.verdict: Accountability requires consent every time its form changes. The Court removes unsolicited coaching from the relationship gym.
templates.move: The frequent coach asks, “support, company, or no input?” The pressured partner answers directly and does not agree to tracking they do not want. Define one welcome encouragement and two off-limits comments.
templates.share: Personal trainer credentials were never filed. ---
templates.headline: COACH WHISTLE CONFISCATED

title: The Shared Calendar Dispute
subtitle: Useful infrastructure or a digital museum of events one person forgot to open?

questions.prompt: Plans currently live in:
Who updates changes?
What needs calendar status?
Optional: Which missed or double-booked plan brought this case to Court?

templates.name: Calendar citizenship
templates.what: Shared plans enter a shared system, changes appear, and nobody must reconstruct the week from reaction emojis.
templates.verdict: The Court recognizes functional calendar citizenship. Continue paying attention to the notifications you requested.
templates.move: `[username A]` adds the next shared plan with details. `[username B]` records the next change rather than announcing it into the air. Review the next seven days in under three minutes.
templates.share: The notification has been sworn in.
templates.headline: CALENDAR CITIZENSHIP

templates.name: One human notification service
templates.what: One person enters plans, remembers birthdays, catches conflicts, and then personally reminds the calendar’s other alleged user.
templates.verdict: A shared calendar maintained by one person is a calendar-shaped assistant job. Update responsibility must follow the person making the plan or change.
templates.move: The less active user adds their next three commitments and sets their own alerts. The maintainer stops issuing duplicate reminders unless requested. Agree that whoever creates or changes a plan updates it.
templates.share: Push notifications will now push themselves.
templates.headline: ONE HUMAN NOTIFICATION SERVICE

templates.name: Multiple timelines detected
templates.what: Plans exist across memory, texts, screenshots, and possibly a calendar last opened during onboarding.
templates.verdict: The issue is not memory quality; it is lack of one trusted source. The Court orders migration before another double booking.
templates.move: One partner creates the shared system and categories. The other imports upcoming commitments and confirms which alerts they will actually notice. Do a fifteen-minute calendar reset, then retire competing systems for shared plans.
templates.share: Timeline merge completed with minor emotional downtime. ---
templates.headline: MULTIPLE TIMELINES DETECTED

title: Who Texts the Group Chat to Plan Things
subtitle: Who keeps asking “so what are we doing?” while everyone else votes with a thumbs-up?

questions.prompt: Who usually starts social plans?
Which part is hardest?
What role do you prefer?
Optional: Which planning job feels most invisible?

templates.name: Social planning duo
templates.what: Plans move from “we should” to an actual time because both people touch the process.
templates.verdict: The Court finds shared social labor and unusually responsive group-chat behavior.
templates.move: `[username A]` starts the next invite. `[username B]` closes the loop with time, place, or reservation. Plan one simple outing using only three messages each.
templates.share: The poll may finally rest.
templates.headline: SOCIAL PLANNING DUO

templates.name: Organizer plus reliable deputy
templates.what: One person naturally conducts the group chat. The other does not lead but provides decisions, confirmations, and actual useful backup.
templates.verdict: Different roles can be fair when the deputy is real, not ceremonial. Keep the organizer out of follow-up-message purgatory.
templates.move: The organizer delegates one concrete step instead of doing it automatically. The deputy completes that step before being reminded. Split the next plan into invite, logistics, and confirmation.
templates.share: Committee structure approved; meeting avoided.
templates.headline: ORGANIZER PLUS RELIABLE DEPUTY

templates.name: One unpaid event coordinator
templates.what: One person initiates, polls, reserves, confirms, and then receives “what time again?” from the person seated beside them.
templates.verdict: Enjoying plans without sharing any planning is a convenience, not a personality type. The Court rotates ownership of the next outing.
templates.move: The usual passenger plans the next social event end to end. The usual organizer supplies constraints once and resists taking the wheel back. Alternate full ownership for the next two plans.
templates.share: “Keep me posted” has been denied as a complete contribution. ---
templates.headline: ONE UNPAID EVENT COORDINATOR

title: The Trash Day Amnesia Case
subtitle: The bins know the schedule. Why does the household remain surprised every week?

questions.prompt: Who notices trash day?
Which step gets missed?
Best fix?
Optional: Which trash-related sequel keeps getting greenlit?

templates.name: Bins under control
templates.what: Trash exits on schedule, bags reappear, and the bins return from curbside travel.
templates.verdict: The household sanitation system is functional. Maintain it with the humility appropriate to this achievement.
templates.move: `[username A]` handles the next forgotten micro-step. `[username B]` checks supplies before the last bag becomes a crisis. Tie the task to one existing weekly habit.
templates.share: The bins have rolled back into civilian life.
templates.headline: BINS UNDER CONTROL

templates.name: One sanitation department
templates.what: One person has become calendar, collector, bag replacer, and curbside operations manager.
templates.verdict: Taking out one full bag after being asked is not the same as owning trash day. Full-cycle responsibility transfers next week.
templates.move: The new owner handles gathering through bin return. The usual owner does not issue reminders; the phone may accept that burden. Assign a permanent owner or visible weekly rotation.
templates.share: Reminder services discontinued due to unpaid labor.
templates.headline: ONE SANITATION DEPARTMENT

templates.name: Recurring waste-management thriller
templates.what: Both people intend to handle it, each completes a different fragment, and the ending still features an approaching truck.
templates.verdict: Good intentions require one named finish line. The Court separates indoor collection from outdoor timing and assigns both.
templates.move: One partner owns all indoor bags and replacements. The other owns curb, pickup timing, and bin return. Set one shared alert with both roles written in the title.
templates.share: Plot hole sealed with a fresh liner. --- # Conflict Court
templates.headline: RECURRING WASTE-MANAGEMENT THRILLER

title: The Leaving-on-Read Trial
subtitle: A message sat unanswered. Busy moment, needed space, or silence carrying extra meaning?

questions.prompt: When you cannot reply, what is usually true?
When they do not reply, what do you feel first?
What signal would help?
Optional: What did the unanswered message mean to you in that moment?

templates.name: Low-stakes timing gap
templates.what: A message waited longer than one person expected, but neither testimony points to a larger pattern.
templates.verdict: This looks like timing, not a hidden statement about the relationship. A tiny status signal can prevent unnecessary lore.
templates.move: The slower replier sends a brief status when practical. The waiting partner allows ordinary delay without opening a second case in their imagination. Choose one phrase that means “I saw this and will return.”
templates.share: Read receipts remain emotionally unqualified evidence.
templates.headline: LOW-STAKES TIMING GAP

templates.name: Silence means different things
templates.what: One person experiences silence as neutral processing. The other experiences the same gap as uncertainty or disconnection.
templates.verdict: Neither meaning is automatic. The relationship needs a shared translation for busy, space, and unresolved conflict.
templates.move: The person going quiet names which state they are in and gives a realistic return point. The other respects that window and saves additional messages for new information. Define three signals: busy, need space, ready to talk.
templates.share: Silence now requires captions.
templates.headline: SILENCE MEANS DIFFERENT THINGS

templates.name: Avoidance loop
templates.what: Important messages repeatedly disappear into long gaps, while follow-ups become more urgent and the original issue remains untouched.
templates.verdict: Space can support a conversation; indefinite silence replaces it. The Court orders a pause with an end point, not instant resolution.
templates.move: The withdrawing partner gives a return time they can keep. The pursuing partner asks once for confirmation and does not use the waiting window to expand the case. Use a repair script: “I need ___ time. I am not leaving. Let’s return at ___.”
templates.share: Pause granted; disappearance denied. ---
templates.headline: AVOIDANCE LOOP

title: The Ex Still Follows You Case
subtitle: An ex remains in the digital orbit. Harmless history, unclear contact, or a boundary needing daylight?

questions.prompt: Current contact is:
What feels uncomfortable, if anything?
What would help most?
Optional: What behavior—not identity or history—makes this feel relevant now?

templates.name: History, not a current issue
templates.what: An old connection remains visible, but the evidence does not show active interference in the current relationship.
templates.verdict: A follow is not a confession. The Court finds history in the algorithm and no automatic threat in the present.
templates.move: The person with the history answers reasonable factual questions once. The concerned partner receives the answer without turning the ex into a recurring background character. Name what current behavior makes trust feel strong today.
templates.share: The algorithm has no relationship jurisdiction.
templates.headline: HISTORY, NOT A CURRENT ISSUE

templates.name: Context gap
templates.what: The contact itself may be ordinary, but one person has been filling missing context with increasingly elaborate possibilities.
templates.verdict: Transparency can reduce mystery without creating surveillance. The useful facts are frequency, purpose, and whether anything is being hidden.
templates.move: The partner with contact shares relevant context before it becomes a discovery. The other asks directly for the information they need rather than monitoring around the edges. Agree on which kinds of ex contact deserve a heads-up.
templates.share: Context admitted; detective work retired.
templates.headline: CONTEXT GAP

templates.name: Boundary conversation required
templates.what: At least one person experiences the current contact as secretive, emotionally central, or outside the relationship’s understood limits.
templates.verdict: The Court will not make a universal ex rule. It will require a specific agreement based on behavior, privacy, and the commitments you actually made.
templates.move: One partner states what contact they want to continue and why. The other states the precise boundary needed to remain comfortable, without demanding erasure of a whole past. Write one mutual rule covering private messages, emotional support, and disclosure.
templates.share: The past may exist; the present gets a vote. ---
templates.headline: BOUNDARY CONVERSATION REQUIRED

title: Emotional Cheating Hearing
subtitle: A friendship feels emotionally central. Supportive connection or intimacy bypassing the relationship?

questions.prompt: What is being shared outside the relationship?
What makes it feel different?

options.label: Turning to them before my partner

questions.prompt: What would restore clarity?
Optional: Which behavior changed the meaning of this friendship for you?

templates.name: Friendship with clear edges
templates.what: The friendship provides normal support and neither person reports secrecy, romantic framing, or displacement.
templates.verdict: Closeness outside a couple is not automatically betrayal. Healthy relationships can contain other meaningful people with understandable boundaries.
templates.move: The friend-connected partner keeps ordinary transparency. The concerned partner identifies one reassurance that supports trust without policing friendship. Name what makes an outside friendship feel included rather than hidden.
templates.share: Friendship remains legal; secrecy remains under review.
templates.headline: FRIENDSHIP WITH CLEAR EDGES

templates.name: Emotional priority drift
templates.what: One outside connection has become the first destination for thoughts, comfort, or private processing that the relationship rarely receives.
templates.verdict: This is less about banning a friend than noticing where intimacy is flowing. The couple needs a deliberate route back to each other.
templates.move: The externally focused partner brings one meaningful topic back into the relationship before outsourcing it. The other creates space to receive it without immediate correction or interrogation. Schedule one weekly check-in for the kind of conversation that has been happening elsewhere.
templates.share: Emotional traffic rerouted, not closed.
templates.headline: EMOTIONAL PRIORITY DRIFT

templates.name: Trust repair required
templates.what: Relevant contact, feelings, or context was hidden, minimized, or framed differently depending on who was asking.
templates.verdict: The central issue is not the label “emotional cheating”; it is whether agreed trust was bypassed. Repair needs accurate disclosure and a boundary both people knowingly choose.
templates.move: The person who concealed information provides the relevant truth without drip-feeding. The hurt partner states what is needed for repair and what cannot be promised away today. Agree on immediate boundaries and a later review point; avoid forcing instant forgiveness.
templates.share: Honesty remains the least dramatic route forward. ---
templates.headline: TRUST REPAIR REQUIRED

title: The Phone Snooping Verdict
subtitle: Reassurance request, privacy collision, or trust issue seeking evidence in the wrong place?

questions.prompt: Phone access in your relationship is:
What prompted this case?
What would help most?
Optional: What need were you trying to meet—privacy, reassurance, truth, or safety?

templates.name: Privacy values align
templates.what: Both people understand what is private, what is practically shared, and what openness means when it is freely chosen.
templates.verdict: Trust does not require identical phone habits. Your rule works because both people recognize it as consent, not proof collection.
templates.move: Each person restates one privacy boundary and one form of voluntary openness they are comfortable offering. Review practical access—emergency contacts, photos, navigation—without turning it into unrestricted inspection.
templates.share: The phone is not a courtroom exhibit by default.
templates.headline: PRIVACY VALUES ALIGN

templates.name: Reassurance and privacy collide
templates.what: One person believes access would settle uncertainty. The other experiences that access as loss of ordinary personal space.
templates.verdict: Surveillance cannot create durable reassurance, and “privacy” cannot end every reasonable question. The need must be answered more directly.
templates.move: The reassurance-seeking partner names the exact concern without requesting an unlimited search. The privacy-seeking partner answers that concern clearly and offers one voluntary, bounded reassurance. Write a phone rule covering permission, notifications, photos, and emergencies.
templates.share: Trust may ask questions; it may not execute a warrant.
templates.headline: REASSURANCE AND PRIVACY COLLIDE

templates.name: Trust breach on either side
templates.what: Privacy was crossed, important truth was concealed, or both happened in the same unhappy sequence.
templates.verdict: One breach does not cancel the other. Repair requires separate ownership: what was hidden, what was searched, and what each damaged.
templates.move: The person who snooped owns that choice without using discovery as retroactive permission. The person who concealed relevant information answers for that choice without using privacy to erase impact. Decide immediate boundaries and whether trust repair needs time or outside support.
templates.share: Two issues separated; neither swept under the screen protector. ---
templates.headline: TRUST BREACH ON EITHER SIDE

title: The In-Laws Boundary Case
subtitle: Family involvement is affecting the relationship. Support, habit, or too many hands on the steering wheel?

questions.prompt: Family is involved in:
What feels hardest?

options.label: My partner not backing me up

questions.prompt: What boundary would help?
Optional: Which family moment made you feel supported—or outnumbered?

templates.name: Family included, couple centered
templates.what: Family is present without running the relationship’s board meetings. Both partners still experience the couple as the decision-making center.
templates.verdict: The Court approves connection with healthy jurisdiction. Keep advice optional and plans confirmable.
templates.move: Each partner thanks one helpful family contribution and names one area that remains the couple’s decision. Agree on what news is shared freely and what requires both people’s okay.
templates.share: Family welcome; voting rights limited.
templates.headline: FAMILY INCLUDED, COUPLE CENTERED

templates.name: Boundary needs a spokesperson
templates.what: The couple mostly agrees on the line, but the line becomes blurry when one family applies pressure in real time.
templates.verdict: A boundary communicated only by the in-lawed partner can feel like personal rejection. The directly connected partner needs to carry the message.
templates.move: The family-connected partner states the shared boundary using “we.” The other avoids becoming the visible enforcer unless direct disrespect occurs. Rehearse one sentence for invitations, advice, and private questions.
templates.share: Diplomatic credentials issued to the correct household.
templates.headline: BOUNDARY NEEDS A SPOKESPERSON

templates.name: Couple authority is being bypassed
templates.what: Private conflict, money, housing, parenting, or major plans are being shaped by family without both partners’ agreement.
templates.verdict: Support can be valuable; outside authority over the couple is a different arrangement. The pair must decide what information and decisions leave the room.
templates.move: The partner whose family is involved pauses new commitments and communicates the limit. The other states the impact and desired boundary without demanding family cutoff as the first move. Create a couple-first rule for major decisions and a plan for handling pushback.
templates.share: Holidays remain advanced-level diplomacy. ---
templates.headline: COUPLE AUTHORITY IS BEING BYPASSED

title: Different 5-Year Plan Hearing
subtitle: Two futures are on the table. Which differences are timing, and which change the destination?

questions.prompt: Biggest uncertainty is:
Your desired timing feels:

options.label: I am unsure I want it

questions.prompt: What do you need now?
Optional: Which future choice feels hardest to compromise without losing yourself?

templates.name: Same destination, adjustable route
templates.what: The horizon looks similar from both seats. The disagreements live mostly in dates, routes, and whose spreadsheet gets opened first.
templates.verdict: You do not need a complete five-year contract. You need the next shared decision and permission to update the map.
templates.move: Each names one commitment for the next twelve months and one assumption still open to change. Build a one-year plan with a review date instead of solving all five years tonight.
templates.share: Future aligned; crystal ball returned.
templates.headline: SAME DESTINATION, ADJUSTABLE ROUTE

templates.name: Timing or route mismatch
templates.what: Both people recognize parts of the same future, but the order, location, career cost, or pace is not equally workable.
templates.verdict: “Eventually” can conceal a real timing conflict. The Court orders dates, dependencies, and tradeoffs into the conversation without forcing an immediate promise.
templates.move: The faster-moving partner names the latest timeline that remains honest for them. The slower or differently routed partner names what must happen before commitment becomes realistic. Compare two plausible timelines and identify the first decision point.
templates.share: Route recalculation permitted; destination still under joint review.
templates.headline: TIMING OR ROUTE MISMATCH

templates.name: Different destination
templates.what: A core future—children, marriage, location, lifestyle, or career structure—matters deeply to one person and is not desired by the other.
templates.verdict: This is not a communication glitch to be solved with better phrasing. Care can be real while future requirements remain incompatible.
templates.move: Each states the need without offering a hopeful maybe they cannot sustain. Each listens for the actual answer rather than negotiating with potential. Decide whether this needs time, a decision date, or support beyond the app; do not force a twenty-minute verdict.
templates.share: No life plan has been sentenced to false agreement. ---
templates.headline: DIFFERENT DESTINATION

title: Gaslighting Accusation Court
subtitle: A disagreement has made someone doubt their memory or reality. What happened around the facts and the impact?

questions.prompt: The disagreement is about:

options.label: A repeated pattern of reality being rewritten

questions.prompt: When you bring evidence or impact, the response is:
What would help now?
Optional: Describe one concrete example without sharing identifying or unsafe details.

templates.name: Memory mismatch
templates.what: Both people remember the event differently, and neither account alone resolves what was said or intended.
templates.verdict: Memory is imperfect; impact still happened. The Court does not need one person to surrender their reality in order to make a repair.
templates.move: Each gives one concrete recollection and one impact statement without declaring the other dishonest. Each acknowledges what can be true in the other account. Agree on the fact you share, the detail you do not, and what should happen differently next time.
templates.share: Certainty unavailable; respect still required.
templates.headline: MEMORY MISMATCH

templates.name: Dismissal pattern
templates.what: The conflict is no longer only about memory. One person repeatedly leaves the conversation feeling foolish, dramatic, or unsure they are allowed to trust their own experience.
templates.verdict: Whether the label “gaslighting” fits is not the Court’s decision. Repeated dismissal is enough reason to change how this conversation happens.
templates.move: The minimizing partner stops debating the legitimacy of the feeling and responds to one concrete impact. The affected partner records examples for their own clarity and chooses a boundary for conversations that become destabilizing. Use a written recap after one important conversation, only if both people can do so safely.
templates.share: The label remains unruled; the impact is officially on the record.
templates.headline: DISMISSAL PATTERN

templates.name: Safety/coercion concern
templates.what: The answers suggest fear, control, retaliation, isolation, or a repeated campaign to undermine one person’s confidence in their own reality.
templates.verdict: The Court is ending the bit. A couple’s quiz cannot safely adjudicate coercion or abuse, and joint confrontation may not be the right next move.
templates.move: The person feeling unsafe prioritizes private support from someone trusted or an appropriate professional resource. The app does not instruct them to disclose plans, confront, or negotiate in a way that could increase risk. None required. Safety does not require a joint exercise.
templates.share: Playful ruling withheld. Your safety matters more than the format. ---
templates.headline: SAFETY/COERCION CONCERN

title: The Jealous of Coworker Case
subtitle: A work connection is activating jealousy. Which facts, reassurances, and boundaries would help?

questions.prompt: What is happening?
What drives the jealousy?
What would help?
Optional: Name the behavior that matters without judging the coworker as a person.

templates.name: Work connection, manageable feeling
templates.what: The work relationship appears ordinary; the jealousy is real but not currently supported by concealed behavior.
templates.verdict: Feelings may request reassurance without appointing themselves investigator. A small amount of context can settle this without policing a workplace.
templates.move: The work-connected partner offers relevant context voluntarily. The jealous partner names the reassurance they need and avoids monitoring or attacking a third person. Agree on one easy check-in after work events.
templates.share: The office group chat has no relationship jurisdiction.
templates.headline: WORK CONNECTION, MANAGEABLE FEELING

templates.name: Specific boundary needed
templates.what: One identifiable behavior—not the coworker’s existence—is creating discomfort: private late-night messages, flirtatious tone, excluded social plans, or missing context.
templates.verdict: Specific behavior can receive a specific agreement. Blanket restrictions and vague “just trust me” answers are both too blunt.
templates.move: One partner describes the behavior and impact without demanding workplace isolation. The other proposes a boundary they can genuinely follow and a reassurance that remains voluntary. Write one work-social rule and one thing that remains normal professional freedom.
templates.share: Boundary tailored; coworker not tried in absentia.
templates.headline: SPECIFIC BOUNDARY NEEDED

templates.name: Trust strain
templates.what: Secrecy, flirting, changing stories, or repeated dismissal has made the coworker a symbol of a broader trust problem.
templates.verdict: Removing one person from the contact list would not automatically repair the pattern. The relationship needs truth, ownership, and observable follow-through.
templates.move: The partner whose behavior created uncertainty answers relevant questions without drip-feeding. The other states the condition needed for continued trust and allows time to verify change. Set one boundary, one transparency practice, and a review date.
templates.share: The symbol has been separated from the actual issue. ---
templates.headline: TRUST STRAIN

title: Moving In Too Fast Trial
subtitle: Exciting next step or several unresolved logistics wearing a cute apartment key?

questions.prompt: What is driving the timing?
Which topic is least settled?
Your current readiness is:
Optional: What would need to be true before sharing an address feels safe?

templates.name: Ready with open eyes
templates.what: Both people want the move and can discuss money, mess, privacy, and logistics without replacing details with “it’ll work out.”
templates.verdict: The Court finds informed enthusiasm. Romance may pack the first box; a written household plan should pack the second.
templates.move: Each owns one pre-move task and discloses one habit the other should not discover beside an unpacked sink. Complete a money, chores, guests, alone-time, and exit-plan checklist.
templates.share: Lease discussion approved; impulse signature not required.
templates.headline: READY WITH OPEN EYES

templates.name: Same goal, different runway
templates.what: Both people can imagine sharing a home, but one needs more savings, information, time, or evidence about daily compatibility.
templates.verdict: “Not yet” can be a path rather than rejection when it contains real conditions and a review date.
templates.move: The more ready partner stops converting excitement into urgency. The less ready partner names measurable conditions and a realistic time to revisit them. Run a short trial—extended stay, shared budget exercise, or chore week—without treating it as automatic consent.
templates.share: Runway extended; destination still possible.
templates.headline: SAME GOAL, DIFFERENT RUNWAY

templates.name: Pressure is driving the move
templates.what: Money, housing urgency, fear, or relationship momentum is pushing faster than one person’s actual readiness.
templates.verdict: Moving in is not a reassurance test. Consent to a shared home must survive the possibility of saying “not now.”
templates.move: The hesitant partner states the no or not-yet clearly. The other helps separate the housing problem from the relationship decision and does not punish the boundary. List alternative housing or timing options before discussing commitment again.
templates.share: Nobody is sentenced to sign a lease tonight. ---
templates.headline: PRESSURE IS DRIVING THE MOVE

title: Unequal Effort Court
subtitle: One person feels they are carrying more. Which labor is visible, and which has gone missing from the count?

questions.prompt: Where is the biggest imbalance?
Is the imbalance:
What is needed first?

options.label: Lower expectations during a hard season

questions.prompt: Optional: Name one piece of effort you want understood, not merely scored.

templates.name: Different work, mutually recognized
templates.what: The contributions are not identical, but both people can name what the other carries and why the current season looks this way.
templates.verdict: Fairness is not symmetry when capacity differs. Recognition plus consent keeps a temporary imbalance from becoming silent debt.
templates.move: Each names one contribution they rely on from the other. Each also identifies one load that should be reviewed if the season continues. Schedule a brief capacity check two weeks from now.
templates.share: The Court cannot count love, but it can notice labor.
templates.headline: DIFFERENT WORK, MUTUALLY RECOGNIZED

templates.name: One load is too heavy
templates.what: Both testimonies point to one person carrying more practical or emotional responsibility than they can comfortably sustain.
templates.verdict: Good reasons may explain the imbalance; they do not make the overloaded person infinitely expandable. One concrete load must move.
templates.move: The overloaded partner chooses the task or responsibility with highest relief value. The other owns it fully or helps secure outside support, including the noticing and follow-through. Transfer one complete responsibility for seven days and review the difference.
templates.share: Capacity limit recognized before system failure.
templates.headline: ONE LOAD IS TOO HEAVY

templates.name: Two invisible ledgers
templates.what: Both people feel they give more. Each ledger contains real entries, but the categories and exchange rates do not match.
templates.verdict: This is not solved by proving whose list is longer. The Court orders shared definitions, priority loads, and fewer unspoken trades.
templates.move: Each lists three recurring contributions and circles the one they most need recognized. Then each chooses one item from the other list to share or reduce. Build a one-week responsibility map without assigning relationship points.
templates.share: Competing ledgers merged; winner column deleted. ---
templates.headline: TWO INVISIBLE LEDGERS

title: The Different Political Views Case
subtitle: Different opinions, different values, or a disagreement changing how safe and respected the relationship feels?

questions.prompt: The disagreement is mostly about:
Conversations usually end with:
What boundary is needed?
Optional: Which difference can you live with, and which touches a core value?

templates.name: Difference with respect
templates.what: You disagree without turning the other person into a caricature. Curiosity remains present and nobody’s humanity is treated as debate material.
templates.verdict: The Court allows political difference where respect and shared life remain intact. Agreement is not the only evidence of listening.
templates.move: Each summarizes the other’s view in terms they accept before offering a response. Each names one shared value underneath the disagreement. Discuss one issue with a ten-minute limit and a mutual stop signal.
templates.share: Democracy survives another dinner.
templates.headline: DIFFERENCE WITH RESPECT

templates.name: Debate is crowding connection
templates.what: The topic returns often, tones sharpen, and the relationship begins hosting a panel discussion nobody requested.
templates.verdict: A boundary around frequency and conduct is not avoidance. It is protection against turning every shared moment into a referendum.
templates.move: The frequent initiator asks consent before reopening the topic. The other names what discussion format remains possible instead of using silence as the only boundary. Agree on no-insult rules, time limits, and topics reserved for deliberate conversations.
templates.share: Campaign season officially shortened.
templates.headline: DEBATE IS CROWDING CONNECTION

templates.name: Core-value incompatibility
templates.what: The disagreement affects dignity, rights, safety, family plans, or the respect one person can feel inside the relationship.
templates.verdict: This cannot be reduced to “agree to disagree.” The Court cannot decide compatibility, but it can refuse to disguise a core-value conflict as casual politics.
templates.move: Each states the value and real-life consequence at stake. Each answers whether the relationship can honor that value without expecting the other to become someone else. Decide whether this needs more time, a decision, or qualified outside support; do not force a playful compromise.
templates.share: The issue remains serious; the conversation is now accurately named. ---
templates.headline: CORE-VALUE INCOMPATIBILITY

title: Love Bombing vs Genuine Romance Trial
subtitle: Big affection felt intense. Mutual enthusiasm, mismatched pace, or pressure dressed as romance?

questions.prompt: The intensity feels:
Do words match behavior over time?
What happens when someone says “slow down”?
Optional: Which gesture felt caring, and which—if any—felt like pressure?

templates.name: Mutual high-volume romance
templates.what: The affection is large, the enthusiasm is mutual, and “not tonight” remains a complete sentence.
templates.verdict: Big gestures are not automatically suspicious. Consistency, consent, and room for ordinary days are the stronger evidence.
templates.move: Each names one grand gesture they enjoy and one low-key behavior that builds trust over time. Plan one intentionally ordinary date and see whether the connection still feels good without fireworks.
templates.share: Flowers admitted; consistency promoted to lead counsel.
templates.headline: MUTUAL HIGH-VOLUME ROMANCE

templates.name: Pace mismatch
templates.what: One person is enjoying the speed. The other likes the connection but needs more time, predictability, or room to choose each next step.
templates.verdict: Slowing down is not rejection, and enthusiasm is not automatically manipulation. The test is whether the boundary is respected without persuasion becoming pressure.
templates.move: The faster-moving partner asks before escalating plans or promises. The slower partner names a pace and form of affection that still feels welcome. Agree on one next step and pause larger promises until a set check-in.
templates.share: Romance remains; fast-forward disabled.
templates.headline: PACE MISMATCH

templates.name: Pressure/control concern
templates.what: Affection is paired with guilt, punishment, boundary-pushing, rapid dependence, isolation, or fear about saying no.
templates.verdict: The Court is ending the romantic bit. Grand gestures never purchase access, commitment, forgiveness, or control.
templates.move: The person feeling pressured prioritizes private support and their own safety. The app does not direct joint confrontation where doing so could increase risk. None required. Consent and safety do not need a couple exercise.
templates.share: Playful ruling withheld. A “no” requires no romantic appeal. ---
templates.headline: PRESSURE/CONTROL CONCERN

title: The Breadcrumbing Verdict
subtitle: Intermittent connection, genuinely busy season, or just enough attention to keep someone waiting?

questions.prompt: Plans usually become:
Communication feels:
What clarity is needed?
Optional: Which repeated pattern makes you feel most uncertain?

templates.name: Busy but mutually engaged
templates.what: Life is crowded, but both people initiate, explain changes, and eventually do what they said they would do.
templates.verdict: Infrequency is not breadcrumbing when mutuality and follow-through remain visible. Protect the connection with realistic plans rather than guilt.
templates.move: The busier partner offers one plan they can actually keep. The other accepts the real pace instead of comparing it with an imaginary ideal. Put one low-pressure plan on the calendar with a clear reschedule rule.
templates.share: Busy schedule, full sentence.
templates.headline: BUSY BUT MUTUALLY ENGAGED

templates.name: Inconsistent availability
templates.what: Interest appears, disappears, and returns with enough warmth to restart the question. Neither person has clearly named what they can sustain.
templates.verdict: The Court cannot infer intent from message frequency. It can require availability and expectations to be stated without decorative ambiguity.
templates.move: The inconsistent partner says what contact and commitment they can reliably offer. The waiting partner names the minimum pattern they are willing to participate in. Agree on one plan and one communication standard for the next two weeks, then review the evidence.
templates.share: Tea leaves replaced with calendar entries.
templates.headline: INCONSISTENT AVAILABILITY

templates.name: Indefinite waiting room
templates.what: Plans remain vague, follow-through is rare, and attention returns mainly when one person begins stepping away.
templates.verdict: Whatever the intent, the current offer is intermittent. The receiving person is allowed to decide based on the pattern, not the potential occasionally advertised.
templates.move: The inconsistent partner stops making promises they cannot schedule. The waiting partner chooses a boundary—specific plan by a date, a different relationship structure, or disengagement. Compare the actual offer with the minimum each person needs; do not negotiate with future versions.
templates.share: Crumbs are not a meal plan. ---
templates.headline: INDEFINITE WAITING ROOM

title: The “We Haven’t in a While” Case
subtitle: Physical closeness changed. What context, pressure, and emotional safety need understanding first?

questions.prompt: The change feels:
What may be affecting it?
What would help first?
Optional: What kind of closeness feels welcome right now? Do not include details you would not want processed.

templates.name: Normal season shift
templates.what: Closeness changed alongside stress, health, routine, or life season, and both people can recognize the context without assigning failure.
templates.verdict: Relationships have changing rhythms. The Court finds no requirement to restore a previous frequency before understanding the present one.
templates.move: Each names one form of non-demand affection that feels good now. Each respects that affection as complete, not a promise of escalation. Choose one pressure-free closeness ritual for the week.
templates.share: A season is not a sentence.
templates.headline: NORMAL SEASON SHIFT

templates.name: Different needs, shared care
templates.what: One person misses physical connection more intensely. The other may need different timing, conditions, or kinds of closeness.
templates.verdict: Desire cannot be argued into equality. A useful conversation protects both longing and consent without making either person defective.
templates.move: The higher-desire partner speaks about feeling and connection without turning it into a quota. The lower-desire partner names what is welcome, what is not, and whether any context needs support. Make three lists privately, then compare: welcome, maybe/ask, and not now.
templates.share: Closeness clarified; entitlement denied.
templates.headline: DIFFERENT NEEDS, SHARED CARE

templates.name: Pressure/safety concern
templates.what: The answers suggest obligation, fear, punishment, ignored refusal, pain, or pressure around intimacy.
templates.verdict: The Court is ending the playful format. Consent must be freely given each time and can change at any point; relationship status does not replace it.
templates.move: The person feeling pressured prioritizes safety, medical care where relevant, and confidential support. The app does not direct a joint exercise or disclose their raw input to the partner. None required. Safety and consent come before couple performance.
templates.share: No one owes a performance. ---
templates.headline: PRESSURE/SAFETY CONCERN
